title: Why cats knead with their paws
fact: Kitten behavior from nursing, shows comfort and contentment

dialogue.text: Professor, why do I keep pressing my paws on everything?
Ah, excellent question, Luna! That's called kneading.
When you were a kitten, you pressed your mother's belly to get milk.
So I'm doing it because I'm happy?
Precisely! It's a comfort behavior from kittenhood.
*kneading the desk* I'm kneading too!
Mochi, you're kneading your homework. That's not the same thing.
It feels nice though...

title: Why cats bring dead mice to owners
fact: Cats see owners as incompetent hunters and provide food

dialogue.text: Professor, why do we bring dead mice to humans?
Excellent question! It's actually quite noble.
Cats think their owners are terrible hunters.
We bring them food because we care?
Exactly! We're essentially saying you're incompetent but we love you.
I brought my human a moth once.
Did they appreciate it?
They screamed and ran away. Ungrateful.

title: Why cats sit in boxes
fact: Boxes provide security and reduce stress

dialogue.text: Professor, why do I love sitting in boxes so much?
Ah, the age-old question! Boxes provide security.
In the wild, enclosed spaces protect us from predators.
So it's like a safe fortress?
Precisely! Plus, it reduces stress significantly.
*stuck in a tiny box* Help...
Mochi, that box is clearly too small for you.
But it's MY box now. I must fit.
Professor, why do we hate water?
Our ancestors were desert cats, Luna.
They rarely encountered water, so we never evolved to like it.
But tigers love swimming!
Tigers are the exception. They're basically oversized house cats who don't care.
*falls in bathtub* HELP HELP HELP
See? Exhibit A.
I'm DROWNING! *swimming perfectly fine*

title: Why cats zoom at 3 AM
fact: Crepuscular nature - most active at dawn and dusk

dialogue.text: Professor, why do I get the zoomies at 3 AM?
Ah! We're crepuscular, meaning most active at dawn and dusk.
3 AM is basically our happy hour.
So it's not just me being crazy?
It's scientific! Your body thinks it's hunting time.
*runs into wall at full speed*
Mochi! Are you okay?
*gets up and keeps running* The wall started it!

title: Why cats stare at walls
fact: They can see things we can't - UV light, small movements, insects

dialogue.text: Professor, why do I stare at walls?
You see things humans can't, Luna.
Cats can see UV light and tiny movements.
So there's something on the wall?
Probably a gnat or dust particle. Or nothing. Both are fascinating.
*staring intensely at corner*
Mochi, what do you see?
The void stares back... *slowly turns head*
